bank.name: Biology
bank.subject: General Science & Ability
bank.description: The human body, cells, plants, diseases, vitamins and genetics — the biology essentials for GSA exams.

questions.prompt: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: The cell is the structural and functional unit of life.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP, the cell's energy currency.

questions.prompt: The control centre of the cell is the?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls cell activities.

questions.prompt: The cell wall of plants is mainly made of?
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are composed of cellulose.

questions.prompt: Photosynthesis takes place in which part of the plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: The green pigment in plants that captures sunlight is?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

questions.prompt: The normal body temperature of a healthy human is about?
questions.explanation: Normal body temperature is about 37 C (98.6 F).

questions.prompt: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the body's largest organ.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest gland of the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland in the body.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone.

questions.prompt: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: An adult human has 206 bones (babies have more).

questions.prompt: How many teeth does a normal adult human have?
questions.explanation: A full adult set has 32 teeth including four wisdom teeth.

questions.prompt: Red blood cells are produced in the?
questions.explanation: Haematopoiesis (blood cell production) occurs mainly in bone marrow.

questions.prompt: Which blood component carries oxygen to the body's tissues?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells transports oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which cells of the blood fight infection?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leucocytes) defend against pathogens.

questions.prompt: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O negative blood can be given to patients of any blood group.

questions.prompt: Which blood group is the universal recipient?
questions.explanation: AB positive can receive blood from all groups.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of vitamin C causes?
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from vitamin C deficiency.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of vitamin D causes?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is synthesised by the skin with sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight enables the skin to produce vitamin D.

questions.prompt: Which of the following vitamins is water-soluble?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C and the B vitamins are water-soluble.

questions.prompt: Insulin is secreted by which organ?
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces insulin, which regulates blood sugar.

questions.prompt: Diabetes mellitus is caused by a problem with?
questions.explanation: Diabetes results from insufficient insulin or insulin resistance.

questions.prompt: DNA stands for?
questions.explanation: DNA is deoxyribonucleic acid, the genetic material.

questions.prompt: The structure of DNA is a?
questions.explanation: Watson and Crick described DNA as a double helix.

questions.prompt: Who is regarded as the father of genetics?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel's pea-plant experiments founded genetics.

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes do normal human body cells have?
questions.explanation: Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

questions.prompt: Malaria is caused by a parasite of which genus?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium species cause malaria.

questions.prompt: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit the malaria parasite.

questions.prompt: Dengue fever is spread by which mosquito?
questions.explanation: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes spread dengue and Zika.

questions.prompt: Tuberculosis (TB) mainly affects which organ?
questions.explanation: TB primarily attacks the lungs.

questions.prompt: Which organ filters waste from the blood and produces urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood and produce urine.

questions.prompt: The basic unit of the nervous system is the?
questions.explanation: Neurons are the structural and functional units of the nervous system.

questions.prompt: Which gas is carried by red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells transports oxygen from lungs to tissues.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a function of the liver?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, detoxifies and stores glycogen; pumping blood is the heart's job.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency leads to night blindness and poor vision.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in saliva helps digest starch?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase begins the digestion of starch in the mouth.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants absorb during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in CO2 for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which organ is responsible for pumping blood?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through the body.

questions.prompt: The process by which plants make food is called:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the food-making process in plants.

questions.prompt: The normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: A normal adult reading is around 120/80 mmHg.

questions.prompt: Which disease is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Measles is a viral disease; the others are bacterial.

questions.prompt: The blood pressure is measured with an instrument called:
questions.explanation: A sphygmomanometer measures blood pressure.

questions.prompt: The study of animals is called:
questions.explanation: Zoology studies animals.

questions.prompt: The largest cell in the human body is:
questions.explanation: The ovum is the largest human cell.

questions.prompt: Which gas do humans exhale in the greatest amount?
questions.explanation: Exhaled air is rich in carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: The process of breaking down food in the body is called:
questions.explanation: Digestion breaks down food into nutrients.

questions.prompt: The 'master gland' of the body is the:
questions.explanation: The pituitary controls other endocrine glands.

questions.prompt: Which part of the plant performs photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is a key component of haemoglobin in red blood cells.

questions.prompt: Which disease is spread by the Anopheles mosquito?
questions.explanation: The Anopheles mosquito transmits malaria.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin helps in the absorption of calcium?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption.

questions.prompt: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.explanation: Nephrons filter blood in the kidneys.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls heartbeat and breathing?
questions.explanation: The medulla regulates vital functions.

questions.prompt: The process by which plants lose water through leaves is:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is water loss through stomata.

questions.prompt: Which deficiency causes goitre?
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes goitre.

questions.prompt: The 'diaphragm' is a muscle that helps in:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm drives respiration.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces bile?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile; the gallbladder stores it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a water-borne disease?
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads through contaminated water.

questions.prompt: The scientific study of heredity is called:
questions.explanation: Genetics studies heredity and variation.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is found abundantly in citrus fruits?
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C.

questions.prompt: The smallest blood vessels in the body are:
questions.explanation: Capillaries connect arteries and veins.

questions.prompt: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light entering?
questions.explanation: The iris adjusts the pupil size.

questions.prompt: Which animal is known as the 'ship of the desert'?
questions.explanation: Camels are adapted to desert travel.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is essential for strong bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium builds bones and teeth.

questions.prompt: The 'Alveoli' are tiny air sacs found in the:
questions.explanation: Alveoli facilitate gas exchange in lungs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a unicellular organism?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a single-celled organism.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells are responsible for clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets help blood clot.

questions.prompt: The study of the functioning of the body is called:
questions.explanation: Physiology studies body functions.

questions.prompt: Which cell organelle is known as the 'suicidal bag'?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes digest cellular waste and are called suicidal bags.

questions.prompt: The normal pH of human blood is approximately:
questions.explanation: Human blood is slightly alkaline, around pH 7.35–7.45.

questions.prompt: The smallest bone in the human body is the:
questions.explanation: The stapes, inside the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the human body.

questions.prompt: Which gland secretes the hormone adrenaline?
questions.explanation: The adrenal glands, located above the kidneys, secrete adrenaline.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a type of blood cell?
questions.explanation: Neurons are nerve cells, not blood cells.

questions.prompt: The largest artery in the human body is the:
questions.explanation: The aorta is the largest artery, carrying oxygenated blood out of the heart.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required for the synthesis of clotting factors in the liver.

questions.prompt: The part of the eye that focuses light is the:
questions.explanation: The lens of the eye focuses incoming light onto the retina.

questions.prompt: The DNA is located in which part of the cell?
questions.explanation: DNA is stored in the nucleus, the control centre of the cell.

questions.prompt: The study of plants is called:
questions.explanation: Botany is the study of plants; zoology is the study of animals.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood back to it.

questions.prompt: Which organ is responsible for detoxifying the blood?
questions.explanation: The liver detoxifies harmful substances in the blood.

questions.prompt: Which pigment gives blood its red colour?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin, the iron-containing pigment in red blood cells, gives blood its red colour.

questions.prompt: Which type of teeth are used for grinding food?
questions.explanation: Molars are the flat teeth at the back of the mouth used for grinding food.

questions.prompt: Which hormone increases the level of sugar in the blood?
questions.explanation: Glucagon raises blood glucose levels, while insulin lowers them.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes assemble proteins from amino acids.

questions.prompt: Mendel's experiments on heredity were performed on:
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel studied inheritance using pea plants (Pisum sativum).

questions.prompt: The basic unit of heredity is the:
questions.explanation: A gene is the basic unit of heredity, carrying the instructions for a trait on a chromosome.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements, balance and posture.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is known as the 'kitchen of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts make food by photosynthesis, so they are called the kitchen of the cell.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessel carries blood towards the heart?
questions.explanation: Veins carry blood back towards the heart; arteries carry it away.

questions.prompt: Which disease is caused by a lack of insulin in the body?
questions.explanation: Insufficient insulin production leads to high blood sugar and diabetes mellitus.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is called the 'anti-bleeding vitamin'?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, so its deficiency causes bleeding.

questions.prompt: Which hormone regulates the amount of sugar in the blood?
questions.explanation: Insulin lowers blood sugar; glucagon raises it, keeping the level regulated.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a fungal infection?
questions.explanation: Ringworm is a skin infection caused by fungi.

questions.prompt: The scientific study of insects is called?
questions.explanation: Entomology is the branch of zoology that studies insects.

questions.prompt: Which part of a plant absorbs water and minerals from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots take up water and dissolved minerals from the soil.

questions.prompt: The type of cell division that produces two genetically identical daughter cells is?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two identical daughter cells for growth and repair.

questions.prompt: Which type of cell division produces gametes (sex cells)?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and produces gametes.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme digests proteins in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Pepsin, active in the acidic stomach, breaks proteins into peptides.

questions.prompt: The hardest substance in the human body is?
questions.explanation: Enamel, the outer layer of teeth, is the hardest substance in the body.

questions.prompt: Which organ stores urine temporarily?
questions.explanation: Urine collects in the urinary bladder before being expelled.

questions.prompt: Which gland controls the metabolic rate of the body?
questions.explanation: Thyroid hormones regulate the body's metabolic rate.

questions.prompt: The pigment that gives colour to the skin and hair is?
questions.explanation: Melanin produced by melanocytes determines skin and hair colour.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a hereditary disease?
questions.explanation: Haemophilia, a bleeding disorder, is inherited through genes.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of ribs are present in the human body?
questions.explanation: Humans have 12 pairs of ribs protecting the thoracic cavity.

questions.prompt: Which artery carries deoxygenated blood?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

questions.prompt: Which vein carries oxygenated blood?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

questions.prompt: The largest muscle in the human body is the?
questions.explanation: The gluteus maximus in the buttocks is the body's largest muscle.

questions.prompt: Which type of organism causes typhoid fever?
questions.explanation: Typhoid is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants give out during respiration at night?
questions.explanation: Without sunlight plants respire like animals, releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Which organ of the body is affected by hepatitis?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver, usually caused by a virus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a viral disease?
questions.explanation: Influenza is caused by the influenza virus.

questions.prompt: Which cells of the retina are responsible for colour vision?
questions.explanation: Cones detect colour in bright light, while rods work in dim light.

questions.prompt: The fluid that lubricates the joints is called?
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid reduces friction between the bones in a joint.

questions.prompt: In which part of the female reproductive system does fertilization usually occur?
questions.explanation: The egg is usually fertilized in the fallopian tube before reaching the uterus.

questions.prompt: The normal resting heart rate of a healthy adult is about?
questions.explanation: A resting adult heart beats about 72 times per minute on average.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an airborne disease?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis spreads through droplets in the air when an infected person coughs.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin deficiency causes beriberi?
questions.explanation: Beriberi results from a deficiency of thiamine (vitamin B1).

questions.prompt: The process by which cells release energy from glucose is called?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose to release energy in the form of ATP.

questions.prompt: Which part of the ear vibrates when sound waves strike it?
questions.explanation: Sound waves make the eardrum vibrate, which is the first step of hearing.

questions.prompt: Which hormone prepares the body for emergencies (fight or flight)?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal glands speeds up the heart and prepares the body for action.

questions.prompt: The scientific study of fungi is called?
questions.explanation: Mycology is the branch of biology that studies fungi.

questions.prompt: The scientific name of human beings is?
questions.explanation: Modern humans belong to the species Homo sapiens.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin deficiency causes pellagra?
questions.explanation: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3).

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls voluntary (conscious) movements?
questions.explanation: The cerebrum controls voluntary movements, thought and memory.

questions.prompt: The removal of nitrogenous waste products from the body is called?
questions.explanation: Excretion removes nitrogenous wastes such as urea from the body.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest mammal in the world?
questions.explanation: The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived.

questions.prompt: Which gland produces the hormone that regulates sleep (melatonin)?
questions.explanation: The pineal gland secretes melatonin, which regulates the sleep-wake cycle.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble; the B complex and C are water-soluble.
